articleTitle: EaStMAN: the Edinburgh and Stirling Metropolitan Area Network
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Extending the LAN - High Speed Data Services
abstract: Seven higher education funded institutions (HEIs) are collaborating to construct a high speed metropolitan area network (MAN)-EaStMAN-in the Edinburgh and Stirling region: the universities of Edinburgh, Heriot-Watt, Napier and Stirling, with the Edinburgh College of Art, Moray House Institute of Education and Queen Margaret College. The aim of EaStMAN in the medium timescale is to provide a pervasive ATM network throughout the region which can encompass educational, hospital academic departments, public and private sector partners etc. Considerable benefits are perceived in pursuing the MAN route to improving the communications infrastructure. The MAN is anticipated to reduce costs by sharing compared with if each institution did things alone, achieve better intra- and inter-institution communication, provide early access to high speed networks to stimulate and support multi-media applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Extending the LAN - High Speed Data Services
abstract: MFS Communications Limited offers a wide range of voice, data and video services. These services share the international wide area network (WAN), which links major commercial centres throughout the USA and Europe. This paper provides an overview of the network technologies used for the MFS family of highspeed LAN interconnection services, Metro HLI.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: European ATM initiatives and early results
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Extending the LAN - High Speed Data Services
abstract: The authors present a picture of the rapidly evolving arena of wide area networking in Europe. There is a clear commitment from most European operators to evaluate the potential of ATM both as a high performance backbone and as a key to end-to-end communication solutions, involving the local as well as the wide area. The homogeneous approach in Europe to provide international services involving wide area services suppliers and network equipment manufacturers is paving the way for ATM deployment in Europe. The early results are quite impressive, especially considering the relative low bandwidth of the link required by application when they are singularly considered. This factor will certainly affect the costs of actual deployment, even if a complete cost benefits analysis cannot be fully worked out since tariffs are not yet completely defined for wide area ATM services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Extending the LAN - High Speed Data Services
abstract: Discusses the role of frame relay in LAN interconnection. The two frame relay based services of Energis, Frame Connect and Managed LAN Interconnect, are then considered. The author discusses Frame Connect in particular including its principles, traffic management and application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Extending the LAN - High Speed Data Services
abstract: We have many applications which are difficult to accommodate on the current WANs, though they operate reasonably over LANs. These demanding applications include, unicast, multicast and near-broadcast services. Normally these applications can be made to operate in a small scale over MANs and WANs; larger scale deployment requires resolution of a number of technical and managerial problems which we are starting to understand-but have not yet resolved. Where we have had access to the relevant facilities, we have shown that these demanding applications operate well on an international scale.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ATM in the MAN and the WAN
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Extending the LAN - High Speed Data Services
abstract: The paper presents comment and conclusions drawn from experience gained in real ATM service networks world-wide. After an overview of the market, the work of various companies is discussed; these include: Pacific Bell, BC Tel, GTE, Southwestern Bell Telephone Company and Swiss PTT. The author concludes by discussing the impacts of standards on deployment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Extending the LAN - High Speed Data Services
abstract: The emergence of ATM as a service platform will enable the extension of the LAN in both the geographical and service dimensions. Geographically wire speed extension, bridging, routing and LAN emulation services can be mounted on a common platform alongside existing services such as frame relay and SMDS. These services will be delivered to the desktop bridging the network management gap between user and WAN. The ability of ATM to support voice, video and image services will complete the business solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
